# Checking a design on the board

The emulator runs the same code, but some things only the board can show. When a design is done in the emulator, give the user this checklist, trimmed to what the product uses.

## 1. Build and flash

```
idf.py set-target esp32s3 build      # once per checkout; builds into build/, leaving the emulator's build-emu/ alone
idf.py flash monitor                 # the board's USB-C port appears as /dev/cu.usbmodem... (macOS) or /dev/ttyACM... (Linux)
```

Flashing usually starts by itself over the USB-C port. If it doesn't, put the board in download mode: hold BOOT while connecting the USB cable, then release it and flash. Afterwards, disconnect and reconnect (on battery, power it off and on with PWR) to run the product.

## 2. Look and touch

- [ ] Every screen is the right way up, with the colours of the emulator's screenshots.
- [ ] Text is readable at arm's length, indoors and in daylight.
- [ ] Every button and row is easy to hit with a fingertip, with no wrong neighbour pressed.
- [ ] Swipes and scrolling feel right: they follow the finger and snap, without jitter.
- [ ] Holding a button fills the progress as expected, and releasing early cancels.
- [ ] The board sleeps and wakes as designed, and the waking press does nothing else.

## 3. What the emulator doesn't model

Check each item the product depends on:

- [ ] **CPU speed and cycle timing:** Time heavy work (parsing, crypto, big redraws) on the board; the emulator runs at host speed.
- [ ] **Cache and PSRAM bandwidth:** Check frame rates and large copies on the board.
- [ ] **Radio behaviour (range, interference, roaming, real signal strength):** Join your real networks, including a 2.4 GHz phone hotspot, and walk out of range.
- [ ] **Brown-outs and supply dips:** Run on a low battery with Wi-Fi and audio active.
- [ ] **Flash wear and NVS write limits:** Count storage writes per hour; avoid writing on every event.
- [ ] **Speaker loudness and tone quality:** Listen to every tone on the board, in the case.
- [ ] **Touch feel: finger size, accuracy at the edges, touch through the case:** Use every touch target with a finger on the board, in the case.
- [ ] **Task scheduling: one simulated core instead of two, host threads switched at the FreeRTOS tick, and the kit's own tasks at app_main's priority:** Test task priorities, timing races and core pinning on the board. In the emulator, avoid malloc and printf from tasks above priority 1 that share them with lower ones: a host lock can hang the instance.
- [ ] **Network access follows the host, not the simulated Wi-Fi: sockets work even while the simulated station is disconnected:** Check that the product waits for LCD349_WIFI_CONNECTED before connecting, and recovers when Wi-Fi drops.

## 4. Values the emulator only assumes

These aren't measured on the board yet, so the emulator uses a stand-in for each or doesn't model it. If the product depends on one, measure it on the board:

- Battery discharge curve
- Current draw: active
- Current draw: display_off
- Current draw: light_sleep
- Current draw: off
- Current draw: download

## Reporting back

Ask the user for a photo of any screen that looks different, the exact text of any error in `idf.py monitor`, and anything that felt slow, missed or confusing.
